questions.question: She ______ here since 2015.
questions.explanation: Actions beginning in the past and continuing up to the present with 'since' take Present Perfect Continuous ('has been living').

questions.question: I ______ the Taj Mahal last year.
questions.explanation: Past time markers like 'last year', 'yesterday', 'in 1947' require Simple Past tense ('visited').

questions.question: The train ______ before we reached the station.
questions.explanation: When two actions happened in the past, the earlier past action takes Past Perfect ('had left').

questions.question: The Sun ______ in the east.
questions.explanation: Universal truths and natural laws are always stated in Simple Present tense ('rises').

questions.question: Water ______ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts take Simple Present tense ('boils').

questions.question: By next June, he ______ his degree course.
questions.explanation: Time expressions like 'by next June' denoting completion by a future date require Future Perfect ('will have completed').

questions.question: Look! The bus ______.
questions.explanation: Imperatives like 'Look!' or 'Listen!' indicate an action happening right now -> Present Continuous ('is coming').

questions.question: He usually ______ to school by bicycle.
questions.explanation: Habitual actions indicated by 'usually', 'always', 'often' take Simple Present ('goes').

questions.question: I ______ a strange noise just now.
questions.explanation: 'Just now' takes Simple Past tense ('heard') in PSC questions.

questions.question: He ______ just arrived.
questions.explanation: 'Just' signaling recent completion takes Present Perfect ('has just arrived').

questions.question: When I saw him, he ______ cricket.
questions.explanation: An ongoing past action interrupted by another past action takes Past Continuous ('was playing').

questions.question: They ______ in this house for ten years.
questions.explanation: Duration with 'for ten years' up to now requires Present Perfect Continuous ('have been living').

questions.question: He ______ not finished his work yet.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is commonly used with negative Present Perfect ('has not finished').

questions.question: The bell ______ before I entered the hall.
questions.explanation: Past action preceding another past event requires Past Perfect ('had rung').

questions.question: It ______ since morning.
questions.explanation: Action continuing from morning till now takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been raining').

questions.question: My father ______ a newspaper every morning.
questions.explanation: Regular habitual routine requires Simple Present ('reads').

questions.question: Babies ______ when they are hungry.
questions.explanation: General fact about babies in plural takes base form Simple Present ('cry').

questions.question: I ______ him yesterday.
questions.explanation: Specific past time 'yesterday' requires Simple Past ('met').

questions.question: We ______ to Delhi five years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Ago' always takes Simple Past tense ('moved').

questions.question: She said that she ______ ill.
questions.explanation: Sequence of tenses: past principal clause ('said') requires past subordinate clause ('was').

questions.question: By the time the doctor arrived, the patient ______.
questions.explanation: Earlier past event before doctor's arrival takes Past Perfect ('had died').

questions.question: I ______ English for the last five years.
questions.explanation: 'For the last five years' requires Present Perfect Continuous ('have been learning').

questions.question: Fortune ______ the brave.
questions.explanation: Proverbs are expressed in Simple Present tense ('favours').

questions.question: As soon as he saw the tiger, he ______ away.
questions.explanation: Consecutive past actions joined by 'as soon as' both take Simple Past ('ran').

questions.question: Hardly had he arrived ______ the lights went out.
questions.explanation: Correlative 'Hardly... when' connects past perfect with simple past.

questions.question: No sooner did the bell ring ______ the students left.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner did / had... than' is the correct correlative structure.

questions.question: He talked as if he ______ everything.
questions.explanation: 'As if' expressing hypothetical unreal situation takes past subjunctive ('knew').

questions.question: It is high time we ______ the work.
questions.explanation: After 'It is high time' or 'It is time', a past tense verb ('started') indicates urgent current action.

questions.question: It is time they ______ home.
questions.explanation: 'It is time' followed by a subject clause requires Simple Past tense ('went').

questions.question: I wish I ______ a king.
questions.explanation: Unreal wish takes subjunctive 'were' for all persons.

questions.question: He behaved as though he ______ mad.
questions.explanation: 'As though' expressing imaginary state takes subjunctive 'were'.

questions.question: The match ______ at 4 PM tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Fixed schedule/timetable in the future is expressed using Simple Present ('starts').

questions.question: Prime Minister ______ Kerala next Monday.
questions.explanation: Official planned future schedule can be stated in Simple Present ('visits').

questions.question: I ______ the letter before you came.
questions.explanation: Past action completed before another past action takes Past Perfect ('had written').

questions.question: She ______ from fever for three days.
questions.explanation: Duration 'for three days' continuing now takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been suffering').

questions.question: Oil ______ on water.
questions.explanation: Scientific fact takes Simple Present ('floats').

questions.question: He ______ twenty cigarettes a day before he quit.
questions.explanation: Past habit that ended takes Simple Past ('smoked').

questions.question: I ______ this car since 2018.
questions.explanation: State verb 'have' (possession) cannot be continuous; takes Present Perfect ('have had').

questions.question: She ______ in the garden when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Past ongoing action interrupted by a phone call takes Past Continuous ('was working').

questions.question: While they were playing, it ______ to rain.
questions.explanation: Sudden event interrupting an ongoing action takes Simple Past ('started').

questions.question: The light went out while I ______ dinner.
questions.explanation: Ongoing past activity takes Past Continuous ('was having').

questions.question: He always ______ foolish mistakes.
questions.explanation: Habitual regular tendency takes Simple Present ('makes').

questions.question: I ______ him for a long time.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb; with 'for a long time' it takes Present Perfect ('have known').

questions.question: She ______ Paris three times.
questions.explanation: Life experience up to present takes Present Perfect ('has visited').

questions.question: I ______ my lunch just 10 minutes ago.
questions.explanation: '10 minutes ago' specifies past time -> Simple Past ('finished').

questions.question: The museum ______ at 9:00 AM every day.
questions.explanation: Daily scheduled time takes Simple Present ('opens').

questions.question: Earth ______ round the Sun.
questions.explanation: Universal law takes Simple Present ('revolves').

questions.question: Honey ______ sweet.
questions.explanation: Sensory stative verb expressing a property takes Simple Present ('tastes').

questions.question: I ______ the assignment by tomorrow evening.
questions.explanation: 'By tomorrow evening' indicates completion before a future point -> Future Perfect.

questions.question: Don't disturb him, he ______ his homework.
questions.explanation: Action taking place right at the moment of speaking -> Present Continuous ('is doing').

questions.question: I ______ any letter from him so far.
questions.explanation: 'So far' is used with Present Perfect ('have not received').

questions.question: This is the best film I ______ ever seen.
questions.explanation: Superlative clause taking life experience requires Present Perfect ('have ever seen').

questions.question: Scarcely had the match started ______ the rain came down.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely had...' is followed by 'when'.

questions.question: He ______ in hospital since last Monday.
questions.explanation: Duration starting from last Monday to present takes Present Perfect ('has been').

questions.question: They ______ each other for twenty years.
questions.explanation: Stative verb 'know' with duration takes Present Perfect ('have known').

questions.question: My brother ______ to London next week.
questions.explanation: Personal arrangement in the near future takes Present Continuous ('is going').

questions.question: I ______ never seen such a magnificent sight.
questions.explanation: Present life experience up to now takes Present Perfect ('have never seen').

questions.question: When did you ______ this pen?
questions.explanation: After auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb (V1) is used: 'buy'.

questions.question: He did not ______ to the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Did not' is always followed by V1 base form ('come').

questions.question: By the end of this year, we ______ here for a decade.
questions.explanation: Duration continuing up to a future point takes Future Perfect ('will have lived').

questions.question: She ______ her finger while cutting onions.
questions.explanation: Past punctiliar action takes Simple Past ('cut', where V2 of cut is cut).

questions.question: The dog ______ since morning.
questions.explanation: 'Since morning' requires Present Perfect Continuous ('has been barking').

questions.question: I ______ the book already.
questions.explanation: 'Already' signaling completion takes Present Perfect ('have read').

questions.question: He ______ abroad last month.
questions.explanation: 'Last month' takes Simple Past ('went').

questions.question: I ______ when the bell rang.
questions.explanation: Past ongoing background action interrupted by the bell -> Past Continuous ('was sleeping').

questions.question: Many centuries ago, people ______ that the earth was flat.
questions.explanation: Historic past fact takes Simple Past ('believed').

questions.question: Listen! Someone ______ at the door.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' indicates action happening right now -> Present Continuous ('is knocking').

questions.question: The plane ______ off at 6:30 AM tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Fixed travel schedule takes Simple Present ('takes').

questions.question: I ______ him twice this week.
questions.explanation: Unfinished time period ('this week') takes Present Perfect ('have seen').

questions.question: He died after he ______ ill for a long time.
questions.explanation: Illness preceded death; earlier past action takes Past Perfect ('had been').

questions.question: The patient had died before the doctor ______.
questions.explanation: Later past action takes Simple Past ('came').

questions.question: We ______ our homework before 8 PM yesterday.
questions.explanation: Completion before a specific past point takes Past Perfect ('had finished').

questions.question: They ______ married for twenty-five years.
questions.explanation: State continuing from past to present takes Present Perfect ('have been').

questions.question: He ______ down while running.
questions.explanation: Instantaneous past event takes Simple Past ('fell').

questions.question: The sun ______ brightly today.
questions.explanation: Temporary ongoing state today takes Present Continuous ('is shining').

questions.question: She ______ three novels so far.
questions.explanation: 'So far' indicates action up to present -> Present Perfect ('has written').

questions.question: I ______ to Goa last winter.
questions.explanation: Past point of time 'last winter' requires Simple Past ('went').

questions.question: They ______ badminton every Sunday.
questions.explanation: Habitual regular routine takes Simple Present ('play').

questions.question: Neither of them ______ yet.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular; 'yet' takes Present Perfect -> 'has arrived'.

questions.question: The child ______ because it lost its toy.
questions.explanation: Ongoing reaction in the present takes Present Continuous ('is crying').

questions.question: He ______ a bath when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Past continuous action interrupted by phone -> 'was taking'.

questions.question: I ______ here for over an hour.
questions.explanation: Duration continuing up to now -> Present Perfect Continuous ('have been waiting').

questions.question: Two years ago, he ______ his first business.
questions.explanation: 'Ago' requires Simple Past ('started').

questions.question: The teacher found that the boy ______ a mistake.
questions.explanation: Mistake made prior to the teacher's finding -> Past Perfect ('had made').

questions.question: Who ______ the telephone?
questions.explanation: Historic invention in past takes Simple Past ('invented').

questions.question: It is ten years since I ______ him.
questions.explanation: In the construction 'It is [time] since...', the 'since' clause takes Simple Past ('saw').

questions.question: It has been two weeks since she ______.
questions.explanation: Clause following 'since' denoting starting point takes Simple Past ('left').

questions.question: By this time tomorrow, I ______ in London.
questions.explanation: Future point of time state takes Future Continuous/Simple ('will be').

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds! It ______ rain.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' is used when present evidence indicates an imminent future event.

questions.question: I ______ this mobile phone for three years.
questions.explanation: Possession over a duration up to now takes Present Perfect ('have had').

questions.question: He ______ in the office when the earthquake occurred.
questions.explanation: Action in progress during past event -> Past Continuous ('was working').

questions.question: Wood always ______ on water.
questions.explanation: Scientific constant fact takes Simple Present ('floats').

questions.question: The soup ______ delicious.
questions.explanation: Stative verb of sense takes Simple Present ('tastes').

questions.question: I ______ him yesterday evening.
questions.explanation: Past time marker 'yesterday evening' takes Simple Past ('visited').

questions.question: By the end of this month, she ______ the syllabus.
questions.explanation: Completion by a future deadline -> Future Perfect ('will have covered').

questions.question: When did India ______ independence?
questions.explanation: Interrogative 'did' takes base form V1 ('attain').

questions.question: He ______ coffee every morning.
questions.explanation: Habitual regular routine takes Simple Present ('drinks').

questions.question: She told me that she ______ the movie earlier.
questions.explanation: Earlier past event in indirect speech -> Past Perfect ('had watched').

questions.question: How long ______ you ______ English?
questions.explanation: 'How long' asking about ongoing duration takes Present Perfect Continuous ('have you been learning').

questions.question: I rarely ______ tea in the evening.
questions.explanation: Habitual frequency 'rarely' takes Simple Present ('have').

questions.question: He ______ from high fever since yesterday.
questions.explanation: Ongoing illness starting yesterday -> Present Perfect Continuous ('has been suffering').

questions.question: The ship ______ before help could arrive.
questions.explanation: Earlier past event before help arrived -> Past Perfect ('had sunk').

questions.question: No sooner had the teacher entered the class ______ the students stood up.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had...' correlative takes 'than'.

questions.question: Hardly had she begun to speak ______ the crowd cheered.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had...' correlative takes 'when'.

questions.question: It is high time you ______ to work seriously.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' takes Simple Past subjunctive ('got').

questions.question: She ______ in this school since 2018.
questions.explanation: Duration with 'since 2018' continuing to present requires Present Perfect Continuous ('has been teaching').

questions.question: He ______ here for five years.
questions.explanation: Duration continuing up to now takes Present Perfect ('has lived').

questions.question: I ______ the President last week.
questions.explanation: Past time marker 'last week' takes Simple Past ('met').

questions.question: India ______ independence in 1947.
questions.explanation: Specific historic past year takes Simple Past ('attained').

questions.question: The bell ______ before the teacher entered the classroom.
questions.explanation: Earlier past action takes Past Perfect ('had rung').

questions.question: The train had departed before we ______ the station.
questions.explanation: Later past action takes Simple Past ('reached').

questions.question: By this time next year, I ______ my graduation.
questions.explanation: 'By this time next year' requires Future Perfect ('will have completed').

questions.question: Look! The child ______ down the slide.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' indicates an action occurring right now -> Present Continuous ('is slipping').

questions.question: Listen! Someone ______ the violin.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' indicates action in progress -> Present Continuous ('is playing').

questions.question: Water ______ into ice at zero degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific constant fact takes Simple Present ('freezes').

questions.question: The earth ______ around the sun.
questions.explanation: Universal truth takes Simple Present ('revolves').

questions.question: Honesty ______ the best policy.
questions.explanation: Proverbs are stated in Simple Present ('is').

questions.question: My uncle usually ______ coffee in the morning.
questions.explanation: Habitual frequency 'usually' takes Simple Present ('drinks').

questions.question: I ______ just received your letter.
questions.explanation: 'Just' signaling recent completion takes Present Perfect ('have just received').

questions.question: He ______ not completed the project yet.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' takes negative Present Perfect ('has not completed').

questions.question: When I visited his home, he ______ a novel.
questions.explanation: Past continuous action in progress -> 'was reading'.

questions.question: While she was cooking, the milk ______ over.
questions.explanation: Sudden interrupting past action takes Simple Past ('boiled').

questions.question: The power went out while I ______ dinner.
questions.explanation: Ongoing past activity takes Past Continuous ('was having').

questions.question: It ______ heavily since last night.
questions.explanation: 'Since last night' takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been raining').

questions.question: How long ______ you ______ here?
questions.explanation: 'How long' with ongoing duration takes Present Perfect Continuous ('have you been waiting').

questions.question: I ______ him for more than twenty years.
questions.explanation: Stative verb 'know' with duration takes Present Perfect ('have known').

questions.question: This is the first time I ______ tasted caviar.
questions.explanation: 'This is the first time...' takes Present Perfect ('have tasted').

questions.question: Hardly had he arrived ______ the lights went out.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had...' correlative takes 'when'.

questions.question: Scarcely had the match started ______ it began to pour.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely had...' takes 'when'.

questions.question: No sooner did the bell ring ______ the students rushed out.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner did...' takes 'than'.

questions.question: It is high time we ______ to work.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' followed by subject clause takes Simple Past ('got').

questions.question: It is time they ______ home.
questions.explanation: 'It is time' takes Simple Past ('went').

questions.question: I wish I ______ a bird.
questions.explanation: Subjunctive wish takes 'were'.

questions.question: He talks as if he ______ the owner of the company.
questions.explanation: 'As if' expressing imaginary situation takes past subjunctive 'were'.

questions.question: The Prime Minister ______ Kerala next Tuesday.
questions.explanation: Official planned future schedule is expressed in Simple Present ('visits').

questions.question: The train ______ at 7:30 AM tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Fixed timetable takes Simple Present ('leaves').

questions.question: I ______ my lunch ten minutes ago.
questions.explanation: 'Ago' takes Simple Past ('finished').

questions.question: She ______ three medals in the competition yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' takes Simple Past ('won').

questions.question: They ______ each other since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Since childhood' takes Present Perfect ('have known').

questions.question: Oil ______ on water.
questions.explanation: Scientific fact takes Simple Present ('floats').

questions.question: When did you ______ this car?
questions.explanation: Auxiliary 'did' takes base form V1 ('buy').

questions.question: He did not ______ to the function.
questions.explanation: 'Did not' takes base form V1 ('come').

questions.question: By 2030, scientists ______ a cure for cancer.
questions.explanation: 'By 2030' indicates future point of completion -> Future Perfect ('will have discovered').

questions.question: She cut her finger while she ______ vegetables.
questions.explanation: Past continuous background activity -> 'was chopping'.

questions.question: He ______ from high fever since yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Since yesterday' takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been suffering').

questions.question: The patient ______ before the doctor arrived.
questions.explanation: Earlier past event takes Past Perfect ('had died').

questions.question: After he ______ his dinner, he went for a walk.
questions.explanation: Action completed prior to walking takes Past Perfect ('had eaten').

questions.question: It is ten years since I ______ my village.
questions.explanation: 'It is [time] since...' clause takes Simple Past ('visited').

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds! It ______ rain.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' expresses imminent future based on present evidence.

questions.question: I ______ this laptop for four years.
questions.explanation: Possession over duration takes Present Perfect ('have had').

questions.question: Who ______ the telephone?
questions.explanation: Historic event takes Simple Past ('invented').

questions.question: The sun ______ brightly in the sky right now.
questions.explanation: Action right now takes Present Continuous ('is shining').

questions.question: He always ______ foolish mistakes.
questions.explanation: Habitual regular tendency takes Simple Present ('makes').

questions.question: I ______ here for over two hours.
questions.explanation: Duration continuing up to now takes Present Perfect Continuous ('have been waiting').

questions.question: No sooner had she entered the hall ______ the audience cheered.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had... than'.
